findings.headline: NSF made a new award to the Texas A&M Engineering Experiment Station for AI digital twins of small and mid-sized drinking water systems.
findings.who_decided: National Science Foundation, Division of Civil, Mechanical, and Manufacturing Innovation
findings.quote: The objective of this project is to support research on a new AI-enabled cyber-physical-social paradigm for predicting, managing, and mitigating cascading disruptions in freshwater infrastructure systems.
findings.award: 2640086, $122,169 obligated 2026-09-09, standard grant to 2029-08-31, PI Sudipta Chowdhury

findings.headline: A UT San Antonio engineer published a self-powered flood sensor that scores flood risk on the device instead of in the cloud.
findings.who_decided: The University of Texas at San Antonio, Klesse College of Engineering and Integrated Design
findings.quote: Our system is an off-grid solution. It generates its own power, evaluates flood risk locally right on the device and sends timely warnings without needing external electricity or expensive network lines.
findings.caveat: Already in the record as tx-2026-0141.

findings.headline: Texas A&M engineering researchers described two AI assistants they built for grid operators and hardware designers.
findings.who_decided: Texas A&M University College of Engineering
findings.quote: We have several checks in place, so we're not relying on the LLM alone or simply accepting everything it generates.
